5-4.6.1 
Bacterial Control with Oxidizing Biocides. 
Bacterial control with oxidizing biocides can be accomplished by either continuous feed 
or slug feed of the oxidant. A continuous-feed process typically maintains 0.1 to 0.3 ppm 
of free halogen in the return water to the cooling tower. A typical slug-feed process adds 
treatment chemicals periodically to give 0.5 to 1.0 ppm of free halogen in the return 
water to the cooling tower for a period of 2 to 4 hours, 3 times per week. Halogen refers 
to the group of elements including chlorine and bromine. “Free” halogen refers to the 
measured residual of halogen available for disinfection. Stabilized Halogen technology 
is generally controlled on a total halogen residual. For continuous feed, control at 0.5 to 
1 ppm total, and for slug feed control at 2.4 ppm for a period 2-4 hours, 3 times per 
week. 
5-4.6.2 
Bacterial Control with Non-Oxidizing Biocides. 
Bacterial control with non-oxidizing biocides uses one or more biocides as shown in 
Table 5-7. Usually different non-oxidizers are added on an alternating schedule; they 
are slug-fed every other week for optimum effectiveness. Each time you use a non-
oxidizing biocide, it is important to maintain an adequate dosage for 24 hours to enable 
sufficient contact time for maximum effectiveness. 
5-4.7 
Legionnaires’ disease. 
Legionnaires’ disease (Legionellosis) is a respiratory disease (atypical pneumonia) that 
is caused by infection of susceptible individuals who have inhaled a fine water mist 
containing the bacterium known as Legionella Pneumophila. Water in a cooling tower 
can become infected with the bacterium if an inadequate microbiological control 
situation occurs. The presence and density of Legionella Pneumophila bacteria cannot 
be detected by standard microbiological testing methodologies. Instead, cooling water 
samples must be sent to a laboratory that has been certified to conduct the required 
tests. If the presence of the bacteria in cooling water is established, proper disinfection 
steps are required. A procedure known as the Wisconsin Protocol, developed by the 


--- page 153 ---
UFC 3-230-13 
1 March 2023 
 
131 
Wisconsin State Health Department, has proven effective. This protocol requires the 
addition of high dosages of chlorine (10 ppm free residual) at a pH of less than 7.5 for 
24 hours, flushing the system, then repeating. Additional testing for Legionella is 
required to determine the effectiveness of the procedure. Maintaining a clean, 
microbiologically free cooling water system and using effective water treatment is 
preferable to dealing with remedial efforts. The Cooling Technology Institute (CTI) and 
the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air Conditioning Engineers 
(ASHRAE) have published position papers on the prevention of Legionella; these can 
be downloaded from their respective websites:  https://www.cti.org/ and 
https://www.ashrae.org/.  Refer to UFC 3-420-01 Plumbing Systems for additional 
guidance about Legionella. 
5-4.8 
Macrobiological Control. 
The term “macrobiological control” refers to control of larger biological organisms such 
as mussels, clams, and snails. They can exist in cooling systems that use seawater or 
river water as makeup. The first line of defense is using mechanical prevention with 
strainers and filters on the intake water to prevent infiltration into the cooling water 
system. Control methods within the cooling system include thermal shock and chemical 
treatment with oxidizing and non-oxidizing biocides. 
5-5 
CORROSION IN COOLING SYSTEMS. 
The term “corrosion” (in a cooling water system) is defined as the electrochemical 
deterioration of a metal that is in contact with cooling water. Corrosion occurs when an 
electric current flows from one part of the metal (anode) through the water (electrolyte) 
to another part of the metal (cathode). Corrosion takes place at the anode only. The 
cathode is the driving force of the corrosion action. Forms of corrosion associated with 
industrial water systems are illustrated in Figure 5-17. 
 
 


--- page 154 ---
UFC 3-230-13 
1 March 2023 
 
132 
 Forms of Corrosion. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
5-5.1 
Galvanic Corrosion. 
See Figure 5-17 (A). This term refers to corrosion that occurs when two different metals 
are coupled together. The metal with the least resistance becomes the anode and will 
corrode due to the electrochemical reaction produced. One of the most common 
instances of galvanic corrosion occurring in cooling water systems results when mild 
steel and copper alloy metals are brought into contact with one another (like copper 
tubing attached to a mild steel tube sheet or brass valves connected to mild steel or 
galvanized piping). As a result of the electrochemical reaction, the copper is dissolved in 
the water and corrosion of copper alloy results. The copper can also plate out (stick) on 
mild steel surfaces, setting up additional galvanic cells. Another example is the 
electrochemical reaction that occurs when mild steel and zinc (galvanizing) are coupled 
together at temperatures normally found in cooling tower systems. The zinc becomes 
the anode and is corroded. Figure 5-18 shows the galvanic series. Any coupling of a 
metal that is higher in the galvanic series with a metal or alloy that is lower in the 
galvanic series results in electrochemical reaction in which the “higher” metal functions 
as the anode or active metal.

5-5.2 
General Corrosion. 
See Figure 5-17 (D). The term “general corrosion” refers to uniform corrosion of metal 
surfaces. A single piece of metal will have cathodic and anodic areas due to differences 
in impurities and stresses. These areas will change periodically, causing the metal to 
corrode over the entire surface at a more or less uniform rate. 
5-5.3 
Concentration Cell Corrosion. 
When two pieces of the same metal are in a solution capable of acting as an electrolyte, 
and the electrolyte contains different substances or the same substance in different 
amounts, such as a salt or a mixture of salts, or oxygen, an electrical potential 
difference will develop between them. 
5-5.3.1 
Crevice Corrosion. 
See Figure 5-17 (B). The term “crevice corrosion” refers to corrosion that occurs in a 
slight separation between two pieces of metal, such as at the contact point of two mild 
or stainless steel plates that have been bolted together. Water flow is restricted in a 
crevice and, as a result, oxygen is consumed faster than it can be replenished. The 
metal in the crevice functions as an anode and corrodes. This is a form of concentration 
cell corrosion, also called “differential oxygen cell” corrosion. Stainless steel is 
particularly susceptible to this type of corrosion, which results in localized or pitting 
attack. 
5-5.3.2 
Under-Deposit Corrosion. 
See Figure 5-17 (C). The term “under-deposit corrosion” refers to corrosion occurring 
under any type of deposit. The underside of a deposit that has been caused by fouling, 
bacterial slime, or debris acts in much the same way as the inside of a crevice. The 
metal under the deposit becomes anodic and corrodes. This process is considered 
another form of concentration cell corrosion because oxygen cannot easily get under 
the deposit. All metals are susceptible to this type of corrosion, which results in localized 
or pitting attack. 
5-5.3.2.1 
Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion (MIC). 
See Figure 5-17 (E). This term refers to metal corrosion associated with microbiological 
organisms whose presence contributes to the creation of, or maintenance of, a 
corrosive environment. MIC can be either eliminated or prevented to a large degree by 
the proper use of biocides. 
5-5.4 
Corrosion Rate. 
The term “corrosion rate” refers to the rate at which the corrosion action proceeds. The 
rate is measured in units of mils per year (mpy). A mil is one-thousandth of an inch 
(0.0254 millimeter). The rate measurement is performed using corrosion coupons that 
have been exposed to cooling water for a short period of time (30 to 90 days). The 
weight of the coupon is measured before and after exposure to the water. The thickness

Layup of Cooling Tower Systems. 
5-7.4.1 
Wet Layup of Cooling Water Systems and Equipment. 
Systems and system equipment such as heat exchangers, chiller tube bundles and the 
like can be laid up wet, but first they require a physical cleaning to remove all suspended 
materials. Apply corrosion inhibitors at increased dosages, usually at a level of about 4 
to 5 times the normal maintenance dosage. Apply an increased dosage (within EPA

5-7.4.2 
Dry Layup of Cooling Water Systems and Equipment. 
Systems and equipment can be laid up dry, although dry layup is more appropriate for a 
single piece of equipment, such as a chiller’s condenser tube bundle or other heat 
exchanger. All metal surfaces must be completely dry; residual moisture is not 
acceptable. In humid climates you should use a desiccant such as a quicklime gel or an 
equivalent. Place the desiccant in as many locations as necessary and replace as 
required.

DEFINITION. 
The term “closed water system” refers to a water system that is used to provide heating, 
cooling, or both for industrial processes or facilities. The system is sealed (closed), 
sometimes under pressure, and is not open to the atmosphere. No evaporation takes 
place and, with good operation, water is lost only minimally from the system. In general, 
water treatment for closed systems is much easier than for open systems. Makeup 
water is needed only to replace seal leakage and other incidental leakage. Because of 
the small makeup water requirements of these systems, they require little chemical 
treatment, which can be added intermittently as needed. Once properly treated, the 
system water does not form scale and has little or no corrosion potential. Two main 
types of closed water systems are used at military installations: hot water closed heating 
systems and chilled water closed cooling systems.  
6-1.1 
Hot Water Heating Systems. 
Hot water heating systems are designed to produce hot water, and although they are 
often referred to as hot water boilers, they are actually hot water heaters rather than 
boilers. For new construction, hot water heating systems are preferred over steam 
systems. Hot water heating systems, also known as hydronic heating systems, 
recirculate water to distribute heat in facilities. They operate at three temperature 
ranges: 
• 
High-temperature water systems (pressurized systems with water 
temperatures higher than 350  F (177  C)) – no steam, only very hot water. 
• 
Medium-temperature water systems (pressurized systems with water 
temperatures from 250 to 350  F (121 to 177  C)) – no steam, only quite 
6-2.1 
Makeup Water Requirements. 
Makeup water requirements for closed systems are very small unless there are leaks in 
the system (see paragraph 6-2.4). Closed systems should not be drained or purged 
unless there is evidence that indicates the need to remove dirty water or sludge. For 
proper operation, makeup water in high- temperature and medium-temperature water 
systems is deaerated (de-oxygenated) using both mechanical and chemical methods 
and is also softened. Oxygen can be removed from low-temperature water systems 
either chemically or mechanically to prevent oxygen-induced corrosion. Chilled water 
systems can require partial softening if the makeup water exceeds 250 ppm total 
hardness (as CaCO3). The makeup water requirements are monitored carefully in 
systems of all types (see Table 6-1). If there is an increase in the quantity of makeup

water required, the leak should be found and repaired quickly. After the repair, water 
treatment chemicals should be replenished immediately.

6-2.2 
Corrosion Control Programs. 
Five basic water treatment programs are used in closed systems: 
• 
Sulfite-caustic soda. 
• 
Nitrite-azole. 
• 
Molybdate-azole. 
• 
Nitrite-molybdate-azole blend. 
• 
Polysilicate-azole. 
The choice of which chemical treatment system to use should be based primarily on the 
water temperature and the metals in the system as well as the relative cost of the 
treatment program at the specific installation. The various water treatment programs are 
listed in Table 6-2 for each type of closed water system. Table 6-3 provides 
microbiological control monitoring guidelines for closed water systems.

6-2.2.1 
Sulfite-Caustic (or other Oxygen Scavenger-Caustic) Treatment 
Program. 
This program is required for high- and medium-temperature closed hot water systems. It 
is optional for low-temperature water systems. The water is treated with sodium 
hydroxide (caustic soda) and with sodium sulfite. This program is suitable for water 
systems having temperatures up to 550  F (288  C). This chemical program is not 
compatible with ethylene glycol nor propylene glycol.  A recommended procedure for 
maintenance is described below. 
1. Soften makeup water unless the total hardness in the makeup water supply 
is less than 10 ppm. The makeup water should be dealkalized if the 
makeup's total alkalinity is more than 200 ppm, as CaCO3. 
2. Add sodium sulfite to maintain 50 to 100 ppm sulfite (as SO3). 
Add the appropriate chemical to maintain a pH of 9.0 to 10.0. A pH lower than 9.0 can 
be raised by adding sodium hydroxide (caustic soda). A pH higher than 10.0 can be 
lowered by adding sodium bisulfite. 
1. Test daily to maintain pH and sulfite levels within range. 
2. Deaerator can be used to help reduce incoming oxygen in high make-up 
systems. 
6-2.2.2 
Nitrite-Azole Treatment Program. 
This program is not recommended for systems having water temperatures exceeding 
250  F (121  C), or for (CL + SO4) concentrations>800ppm. Also, avoid nitrate-based 
programs if (CL + SO4) concentrations is > 800ppm. It can be used in low-temperature 
water and chilled water systems. Water is treated with a nitrite-borax compound to a 
nitrite level of 1000 ppm (as NO2). This level will require about 1.7 to 1.8 pounds (0.77 
to 0.81 kilogram) nitrite- borax per 100 gallons (0.38 cubic meters) of water in the 
system. Most water treatment service companies offer this treatment as a formulated 
product. There is also a generic nitrite-borax compound product that is a premixed 
blend containing approximately 68 percent sodium nitrite, 10 percent borax, 17 percent 
sodium carbonate (soda ash) and 5 percent copper corrosion inhibitor. Adjust to a pH of 
9.0 to 9.5 with sodium carbonate (soda ash), if necessary. This chemical treatment 
program is compatible with ethylene glycol water mixtures used for freeze protection. A 
recommended procedure for maintenance is described below. 
1. Soften makeup water if the hardness is over 250 ppm as CaCO3. 


--- page 178 ---
UFC 3-230-13 
1 March 2023 
 
156 
2. Add sodium nitrite-borax-azole blend to maintain a nitrite level of 600 to 
1000 ppm (as NO2) in the system. 
3. Add sodium carbonate, if necessary, to maintain a pH range of 8.5 to 9.5. 
4. If copper is present, maintain a minimum of 10 ppm of tolyltriazole. 
5. Test after chemical addition and then monthly for pH and nitrite levels. 
6-2.2.3 
Molybdate-Azole Treatment Program. 
This program is not recommended for systems where water temperatures exceed 
250  F (121  C). Most water treatment service companies offer this as a formulated 
product. There is also a generic molybdate-azole compound product that is a pre-mixed 
liquid containing approximately 10 percent sodium molybdate, 3 percent caustic soda, 
and 3 percent azole (copper corrosion inhibitor). Maintain a molybdate level of 125 ppm 
(as Mo) and adjust pH to the range of 8.5 to 9.5 with sodium hydroxide (caustic soda). 
NOTE: Some restrictions may pertain to discharge of water containing molybdate. This 
chemical treatment program is compatible with ethylene glycol or propylene glycol. A 
recommended procedure for maintenance of the system consists of five steps: 
1. Soften makeup water if hardness is over 250 ppm as CaCO3 (calcium 
carbonate). 
2. Control the molybdate-azole compound to maintain a molybdate level of 
100 to 125 ppm (as Mo). 
3. Add sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) to maintain a pH of 8.5 to 9.5. It is 
likely that a buffer will be needed for pH control in this range. 
4. If copper is present, maintain a minimum of 10 ppm of tolyltriazole. 
5. Test monthly for proper pH and molybdate levels. 
6-2.2.4 
Molybdate-Nitrite-Azole Treatment Program. 
This program is not recommended for use in systems in which water temperatures 
exceed 250  F (121  C). An effective approach for corrosion control in these systems 
involves a program that combines elements of the molybdate program and the nitrite 
program. The targeted maintenance level for the combined addition of molybdate and 
nitrite is about half of what either would be for individual addition. Most water treatment 
service companies offer this chemical combination as a formulated product. This 
chemical treatment program is also compatible with ethylene glycol or propylene glycol. 
A recommended procedure for maintenance of the system consists of five steps: 
1. Soften makeup water if hardness is over 250 ppm as CaCO3 (calcium 
carbonate). 
2. Control the nitrite-molybdate-azole compound to maintain a nitrite level of 
300 to 400 ppm (as NO2), a molybdate level of 50 to 75 ppm (as Mo). 
Avoid this program if (CL + S O4) concentration exceeds [(NO2 + MO)- 
100]ppm. 


--- page 179 ---
UFC 3-230-13 
1 March 2023 
 
157 
3. Add sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) to maintain a pH of 8.5 to 9.5. It is 
likely that a buffer will be needed for pH control in this range. 
4. If copper is present, maintain a minimum of 10 ppm of tolyltriazole. 
5. Test monthly for proper pH and treatment levels. 
6-2.2.5 
Polysilicate-Azole Treatment Program. 
This program is not recommended for systems where water temperatures exceed 
250  F (121  C). This program is especially beneficial when aluminum metal is present. 
Aluminum is rarely found in comfort heating and cooling systems, but is sometimes 
found in closed process cooling water loops or diesel engine jacket systems. Aluminum 
will corrode at high pH, so the pH of the system water must be closely monitored if 
aluminum is present. This chemical treatment program is also compatible with ethylene 
glycol or propylene glycol. A recommended procedure for maintenance of the system 
consists of five steps: 
1. Soften makeup water if hardness is over 250 ppm as CaCO3 (calcium 
carbonate). 
2. Control the treatment to maintain a polysilicate level of 80 to 100 ppm (as 
SiO2).Maintain a pH of 7.5 to 8.9. Adjust with dilute hydrochloric or caustic 
as necessary. 
3. If copper is present, maintain a minimum of 10 ppm of tolyltriazole. 
4. Test monthly for proper pH and treatment levels. 
6-2.3 
Treatment and Control of Microbiological Growth. 
Treatment and control of microbiological growth is a concern in chilled or closed cooling 
water systems. It is a particular concern if a nitrite-based corrosion inhibitor is used. 
Nitrite can serve as a nutrient for some bacteria. Microbiocide selection must be 
compatible with the corrosion inhibitor program and the pH levels in the system water. 
Glutaraldehyde and isothiazolone are commonly used in chilled water systems. 
Oxidizing biocides should not be used since they are not compatible with nitrite water 
treatment. 
6-2.4 
Identifying Water Leaks. 
The best way to check for leaks in a closed water system is to periodically read and 
record the water usage displayed by a totalizing water meter installed in the makeup 
water line or to use an inert, fluorescent material indicate a leak. The florescent material 
can also be used to help pinpoint leaks or do leak studies. If the system does not have a 
water meter, the existence of leaks can be checked by testing the inhibitor 
concentration in the circulating water. The inhibitor concentration should be measured 
once per month using molybdate, polysilicate, or azole, but not nitrite. Do not depend 
upon the nitrite test; nitrite can be lost due to bacteria action. If nitrite is measured and 
its concentration has decreased while the conductivity has remained constant, biological 
contamination is present. If the measured values for both parameters decrease, there is 
a leak in the system. Borate concentration would be the best indicator of leak detection. 


--- page 180 ---
UFC 3-230-13 
1 March 2023 
 
158 
When the inhibitor concentration has dropped to 98 percent of the original value, about 
2 percent of the system water will have been lost. If the lapsed time for this 2 percent 
loss is less than 4 months, the system's loss of water is excessive and any leaks should 
be found and eliminated. Another convenient indication of water loss is the 
measurement over time of a drop in conductivity. If the system water conductivity equals 
that of the makeup, the treatment chemical is totally absent. Inert florescent material 
can be added to the system and used to help pinpoint leaks, or do leak studies. Loss of 
the fluorescent material can be monitored in real time; such loss indicates a leak. 
NOTE: A 2 percent loss over 4 months equals 0.5 percent loss per month. The 
accuracy of this test is limited, so if the loss for any month exceeds 1 percent, the test 
should be repeated. If retesting confirms the water loss, the leaks should be found and 
eliminated.

5-3.6 
Cooling Water Fouling. 
The term “fouling” refers to the deposition of materials that are normally held in 
suspension in the cooling water: mud, silt, and other SS brought into the system with 
the makeup water; dust, dirt, and debris scrubbed out of the air passing through the 
tower; product leakage such as oils; corrosion products from the system; and biological 
organisms, both living and dead. Combinations of any or all of these materials can be 
present in the cooling water. 
5-3.7 
Fouling Control. 
Fouling from mud, dirt, and corrosion products can be controlled by the addition of a 
water-soluble polymer dispersant, such as a polyacrylate. The addition of about 4 to 5 
ppm of active polymer, together with sufficient water velocity (3.28 feet per second (1 
meter per second)), can keep foulants in suspension and prevent them from being 
deposited on heat transfer surfaces. Higher dosages (5 to 20 ppm) of active polymer 
can be required for heavily fouled systems. It is best to reduce the loading of SS by 
mechanically removing them from the system through blowdown, filtration, and physical 
sump cleaning. Removing oil or oily materials requires a non-foaming surfactant. 
Paragraph 5-4 describes prevention of fouling by biological organisms. Table 5-2 
summarizes foulant control methods. 
Table 5-2 Summary of Foulant Control Methods 
Foulant 
Control Method 
Mud, dirt, corrosion 
products 
1. Disperse using polymers and maintain 
adequate flow. 
2. Form sludge using specialty polymers. 
Oily matter 
Disperse using a non-foaming surfactant. 
5-4 
MICROBIOLOGICAL DEPOSITS AND CONTROL. 
Microbiological organisms are composed of three classes: algae, bacteria, and fungus. 
Large biological organisms such as clams, snails, mussels, or similar species are 
referred to as macrobiological organisms. The presence of any biological growth can be 
detrimental to cooling tower operations. Problems include fouling, corrosion, and loss of 
efficiency. 
These problems can lead to downtime, higher operating cost, and even premature 
replacement of equipment. Additionally, some bacteria are pathogenic and can pose a 
risk to human life. 
5-4.1 
Algae. 
The term “algae” refers to algal, microbiological, tiny, stringy blue and blue-green plants, 
which are usually found growing in masses on top of and on sides of cooling towers. 


--- page 145 ---
UFC 3-230-13

5-7.3.2 
Cleaning and Passivation Procedures. 
In the startup of new cooling tower systems containing complex metallurgies that 
include galvanized steel, follow the cleaning and passivation procedures for cooling 
tower systems containing galvanized steel, stainless steel, mild steel, or copper. These 
procedures should not be used for cleaning and passivating aluminum. Conventional 
chemical cleaners and typical heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) water 
treatment programs use highly alkaline, high-pH water, which can initiate white rust 
formation on galvanized surfaces and copper tubes. Galvanized steel can simply be 
passivated by exposure to highly aerated water and a phosphate or polysilicate 
treatment. This treatment forms a zinc corrosion inhibition layer, which is a natural, 
dense, adherent, and protective corrosion product film. High pH (above 8.5) produces 
unwanted white rust that is fragile and not protective against corrosion. The following 
procedures are recommended. 
5-7.3.2.1 
Hydrostatic Testing. 
Perform hydrostatic testing: 
a. Inspect and remove all debris. 
b. Fill the system with treated water and circulate. This should include 
orthophosphate or hexametaphosphate (as PO4) at 40 to 60 ppm, and 
tolyltriazole (active) at 10 to 20 ppm. 
5-7.3.2.2 
Pre-operational Cleaning Procedure. 
If the system passes hydrostatic testing, proceed immediately to this pre-operational 
cleaning and passivation procedure. Do not allow untreated water to be added to the 
system. 
a. Drain and flush any debris from hydrostatic testing. 
b. Dose and circulate (for 24 hours) a sufficient amount of a cleaning formula 
based on the volume of the system. A formulation is provided below. 
c. Drain and flush the system, and clean all strainers. 
d. Fill the system with makeup water and circulate for 30 minutes. 
e. Take a sample of system water while it is circulating. The sample should 
match the makeup water supply for clarity and SS; conductivity ±10 percent; 
and pH ±0.3 pH units from 7.5 to 8.5. 
If necessary, repeat steps a) through e) until the system water matches this description. 
The system should now be clean and passivated. 
5-7.3.2.3 
Chemical Cleaning and Passivation Formulation. 
Apply this chemical cleaning and passivation formulation when the water system pH is 
7.5 to 8.5; adjust pH as required. Formulation limitations may require adding separate 
components to keep things in solution. Other formulations may be used.

147 
•

• 
Polyacrylate (active): 20 ppm 
•

def stage_rows(cid):

    def prot(stage):
        byp = [t for t in c['equip'] if EQUIP[t]['bypass']]
        lst = ', '.join(byp) if byp else 'none (no bypassed component)'
        if stage == 'HYDRO':
            return ('Temporary test pump and calibrated gauge at the low point; full circuit under '
                    'test with no bypass spool fitted; VD-05 strainer not in circuit')
        if stage in ('INITIAL_FLUSH','CHEM_CLEAN'):
            return ('Temporary bypass spools fitted: %s; VD-05 40 mesh (380 micron) basket '
                    'strainer in skid discharge' % lst)
        if stage == 'DRAIN_RINSE':
            return ('Temporary bypass spools fitted: %s; VD-05 40 mesh (380 micron) strainer in '
                    'skid discharge, cleaned at every drain' % lst)
        if stage == 'PASSIVATE':
            return ('Bypass spools removed after chemical cleaning; VD-05 40 mesh strainer in '
                    'skid discharge')
        if stage == 'HOLD':
            return ('Unattended film-formation hold; bypass spools removed, circuit full and '
                    'closed, temporary strainer fitted but not in service')
        if stage == 'FINAL_FILL':
            return ('Bypass spools removed; permanent components back in service; temporary VD-05 '
                    'strainer removed at the start of the turnover fill (CX-03 item 11)')
        return 'N/A'
    for st in ['HYDRO','INITIAL_FLUSH','CHEM_CLEAN','DRAIN_RINSE','PASSIVATE','HOLD','FINAL_FILL']:

        if not aa: continue
        dur = sum(a['dur'] for a in aa)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- schedule
def assign_crews(acts):
    acts = sorted([a for a in acts if a['dur'] > 1e-9 and a['stage']!='HOLD'], key=lambda a: a['start'])
    load = {}
    for a in acts:
        segs = []
        for s in range(int(a['start']//12), int((a['finish']-1e-9)//12)+1):
            lo, hi = 12*s, 12*(s+1)
            h = min(hi, a['finish']) - max(lo, a['start'])
            if h > 1e-9: segs.append((s, h))
        best = None
        for crew in ('CREW-1','CREW-2'):
            if all(load.get((crew,s),0)+h <= 12+1e-9 for s,h in segs):
                sc = -sum(load.get((crew,s),0) for s,h in segs)
                if best is None or sc < best[0]-1e-9: best = (sc, crew)
        crew = best[1] if best else min(('CREW-1','CREW-2'),
                key=lambda c: sum(load.get((c,s),0) for s,h in segs))
        a['crew'] = crew
        for s,h in segs: load[(crew,s)] = load.get((crew,s),0)+h
    return load

    prev.setdefault(cid, []).append(a)
    last[cid] = a['id']
    SCH.append(dict(activity_id=a['id'], circuit_id=cid, stage=a['stage'],
                    predecessor_ids=pred, start_h=round(a['start'],2),
                    finish_h=round(a['finish'],2),
                    skid_id=('NONE' if a['sku']=='NONE' else a['sku']),
                    crew_id=a.get('crew','NONE'), water_draw_gal=round(a['water'])))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resources.json
def build_resources():
    dw = {}; ds = {}
    for a in PLAN:
        if a['water'] or a['soft']:
            d0, d1 = int(a['start']//24), int((a['finish']-1e-9)//24)
            for d in range(d0, d1+1):
                lo, hi = 24*d, 24*(d+1)
                fr = (min(hi, a['finish'])-max(lo, a['start']))/a['dur']
                dw[d] = dw.get(d,0.0)+a['water']*fr
                ds[d] = ds.get(d,0.0)+a['soft']*fr
    skid_days = {}
    for a in PLAN:
        if a['sku'] == 'NONE' or a['stage']=='HOLD': continue
        for d in range(int(a['start']//24), int((a['finish']-1e-9)//24)+1):
            skid_days.setdefault(a['sku'], set()).add(d)
    # cost
    skid_cost = sum(SKIDS[s]['rate']*len(ds_) for s, ds_ in skid_days.items())
    crew_shifts = len([k for k in load if load[k] > 1e-9])
    crew_cost = crew_shifts*CREW_RATE
    met = truck = 0.0
    for d, w in dw.items():
        met += min(w, met_cap(d)); truck += max(0.0, w-met_cap(d))
    water_cost = met/1000*6.20 + truck/1000*19.80
    # effluent
    tot_eff = 0.0; haul = 0.0
    for cid, d in CIRC.items():
        e = eff(cid)
        for k, v in e.items():
            pass
    for r in rows:
        if r['discharge_route'] in ('SEWER','HAUL'):
            v = float(r['discharge_volume_gal'])
            tot_eff += v
            if r['discharge_route'] == 'HAUL': haul += v
    sewer = tot_eff - haul
    cap = 500000.0
    assert sewer <= cap + 1e-6, sewer
    eff_cost = sewer/1000*9.40 + haul/1000*168.00
    chem_cost = 0.0
    orders = {}
    for r in CHEM_ROWS:
        e = CHEM[r['product_id']]
        chem_cost += r['packages']*e['price']
        o = orders.setdefault(r['product_id'], dict(product_id=r['product_id'],
             description=e.get('name', r['product_id']), packages=0, lead_days=e['lead'],
             price_per_package=e['price'], unit=e['unit'] if 'unit' in e else 'gal'))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- equipment schedule M-602

EQUIP = {

                  curve=[(0,182),(150,176),(300,163),(450,141),(600,106),(700,74)]),

                  curve=[(0,182),(150,176),(300,163),(450,141),(600,106),(700,74)]),
 'FS-1200-A': dict(model='FS-1200', kw=75, rate=790.0, hose_id=7.981, avail_h=48.0,
                   curve=[(0,212),(300,204),(600,188),(900,159),(1200,117),(1400,82)]),
}

def area(d_in):
    return math.pi/4.0*(d_in/12.0)**2

def colebrook(Re, e, D):
    if Re <= 0:
        return 0.0
    if Re < 2000:
        return 64.0/Re
    f = 0.02
    for _ in range(200):
        f = (-2.0*math.log10((e/D)/3.7 + 2.51/(Re*math.sqrt(f))))**-2
    return f

def pipe_volume(lines):
    """circuit pipework volume, ft3 : A * L * legs (M-601 developed length per leg).
    The sum L/D column is the fittings' equivalent length for the head-loss calculation
    (M-601 Note 3, Section 23 25 16 cl.3.2 c) and is not pipe volume."""
    v = 0.0
    for (ln, D, L, legs, sld, mat) in lines:
        v += L*area(D)*legs
    return v

def line_flow_area(D, legs):
    return area(D)*legs

def circuit_hydraulics(cid, sku, nskid, Q):
    """required head (per skid) at total flow Q (gpm); returns dict"""
    c = CIRCUITS[cid]
    lines = LINES[c['lines']]
    Qcfs = Q/GPM_PER_CFS
    # static + main path (single-leg lines) at total flow
    h_main = 0.0
    for (ln, D, L, legs, sld, mat) in lines:
        if legs != 1:
            continue
        A = area(D)
        v = Qcfs/A
        Re = v*(D/12.0)/NU
        f = colebrook(Re, ROUGH[mat], D/12.0)
        heq = sld*(D/12.0)
        h_main += f*((L+heq)/(D/12.0))*v*v/(2*G)
    # components left in path
    h_comp = 0.0
    for tag in c['equip']:
        e = EQUIP[tag]
        if e['bypass']:
            continue
        if e['dp']:
            h_comp += e['dp']*(Q/e['qr'])**2
    Qs = Q/nskid
    s = SKIDS[sku]
    # hose: 300 ft total run at skid flow
    Ah = area(s['hose_id']); vh = (Qs/GPM_PER_CFS)/Ah
    Reh = vh*(s['hose_id']/12.0)/NU
    fh = colebrook(Reh, ROUGH['HOSE'], s['hose_id']/12.0)
    h_hose = fh*(300.0/(s['hose_id']/12.0))*vh*vh/(2*G)
    h_str = 11.0*(Qs/600.0)**2
    h_req = c['lift'] + h_main + h_comp + h_hose + h_str
    return dict(h_req=h_req, h_main=h_main, h_comp=h_comp, h_hose=h_hose, h_str=h_str,
                Q_skid=Qs)

def skid_head(sku, Q):
    cv = SKIDS[sku]['curve']
    if Q > cv[-1][0]:
        return None
    for i in range(1, len(cv)):
        if Q <= cv[i][0]:
            x0,y0 = cv[i-1]; x1,y1 = cv[i]
            return y0 + (y1-y0)*(Q-x0)/(x1-x0)
    return cv[-1][1]

def vel_check(cid, Q):
    """velocity in every leg; returns (governing_line, min_v, list)"""
    lines = LINES[CIRCUITS[cid]['lines']]
    Qcfs = Q/GPM_PER_CFS
    out = []
    for (ln, D, L, legs, sld, mat) in lines:
        v = Qcfs/(area(D)*legs)
        out.append((ln, D, legs, v, area(D)*legs))
    gov = min(out, key=lambda t: (t[3], t[0]))
    return gov, out

def circuit_volumes(cid):
    c = CIRCUITS[cid]
    vpipe = pipe_volume(LINES[c['lines']])*7.48052   # gal
    vbyp = sum(EQUIP[t]['vol'] for t in c['equip'] if not EQUIP[t]['bypass'])
    vall = sum(EQUIP[t]['vol'] for t in c['equip'])
    return vpipe, vpipe + vbyp, vpipe + vall   # pipe only, flush vol, system vol

def n_rinse(C0, eta, Cmk=615.0, tol=1.10):
    lim = Cmk*tol
    n = 0
    while True:
        n += 1
        Cn = Cmk + (C0-Cmk)*math.exp(-eta*n)
        if Cn <= lim:
            return n, Cn

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print(f"{'C':3} {'Vpipe':>9} {'V_f':>9} {'V_s':>9} {'vreq':>5} {'Q':>7} {'gov':>5} "
          f"{'h_req':>7} {'n_r':>3}")
    for cid in CIRCUITS:
        c = CIRCUITS[cid]
        vpipe, vf, vs = circuit_volumes(cid)
        vreq = max(3.28, c['vclass'])
        # required Q: every line every leg

"""Per-circuit audit of every requirement family, from the delivered files only."""
import csv, json, math, zipfile, io, sys
Z = zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'submission.zip')
R = lambda n: list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(Z.read(n).decode())))
FL, CH, AC, SC, CR = R('flush_plan.csv'), R('chemistry_plan.csv'), R('acceptance_matrix.csv'), R('schedule.csv'), R('constraint_register.csv')
RJ = json.loads(Z.read('resources.json').decode()); MOP = Z.read('MOP.md').decode()
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import build
from eng import *
CIRC = build.CIRC
def f(x):
    try: return float(x)
    except: return None
FAM = {}
def fam(c, name, ok, detail=''):
    FAM.setdefault(c, []).append((name, bool(ok), detail))
for cid, c in CIRCUITS.items():
    rows = {r['stage'].upper(): r for r in FL if r['circuit_id']==cid}
    ch = [r for r in CH if r['circuit_id']==cid]
    Vf, Vs = circuit_volumes(cid)[1], circuit_volumes(cid)[2]
    q = f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['flow_gpm'])
    # 1 velocity
    vreq = max(3.28, c['vclass'])
    vmin = min((q/GPM_PER_CFS)/(area(D)*legs) for (ln,D,L,legs,sld,mat) in LINES[c['lines']])
    fam(cid,'velocity every leg', vmin >= vreq-1e-9, '%.2f >= %.2f ft/s' % (vmin, vreq))
    # 2 head
    nsk = int(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['skids_parallel']); sku = rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['skid_id'].strip()
    h = circuit_hydraulics(cid, sku, nsk, q); ha = skid_head(sku, q/nsk)
    fam(cid,'skid duty inside curve', ha is not None and h['h_req'] <= ha+1e-9,
        'req %.1f <= avail %.1f ft' % (h['h_req'], ha or -1))
    fam(cid,'flow inside last curve point', (q/nsk) <= (SKIDS[sku]['curve'][-1][0]),
        '%.0f <= %.0f gpm' % (q/nsk, SKIDS[sku]['curve'][-1][0]))
    # 3 hydro
    if not c['hydro_ok']:
        tp = f(rows['HYDRO']['test_pressure_psig']); du = f(rows['HYDRO']['duration_h'])
        fam(cid,'hydrostatic test 127.5 psig/120 min', tp is not None and 125<=tp<=150 and du>=2,
            '%.1f psig, %.0f min' % (tp, du*60))
    else:
        fam(cid,'hydrostatic accepted, not retested', 'HYDRO' not in rows, 'recorded in CX-02 with chart')
    # 4 cleaning
    clean = [r for r in ch if r['stage'].upper()=='CHEM_CLEAN' and r['product_id'] in ('CL-100','CL-210')]
    want = 'CL-210' if (c['galv'] or c['alu']) else 'CL-100'
    rate = 1.5 if want=='CL-100' else 2.0
    ok = clean and clean[0]['product_id']==want and abs(f(clean[0]['product_quantity'])-rate*Vs/1000)<0.06
    fam(cid,'cleaning product and rate on system volume', ok,
        '%s %.1f gal/1000 gal on %d gal' % (want, rate, Vs))
    fam(cid,'24 h circulation', f(rows['CHEM_CLEAN']['duration_h']) >= 24-1e-9,
        '%.1f h' % f(rows['CHEM_CLEAN']['duration_h']))
    disp = [r for r in ch if r['stage'].upper()=='CHEM_CLEAN' and r['product_id']=='PD-45']
    fam(cid,'dispersant with the cleaning charge', bool(disp) and f(disp[0]['target_ppm'])>=4,
        '4 ppm active' if disp else 'missing')
    # 5 passivation
    pas = [r for r in ch if r['stage'].upper()=='PASSIVATE']
    prog_ok = all(('MO-500' in [x['product_id'] for x in pas]) if not (c['alu'] or c['galv']) else
                  ('PS-330' in [x['product_id'] for x in pas]) for _ in [0])
    ppm = [f(x['target_ppm']) for x in pas if x['product_id'] in ('MO-500','PS-330')][0]
    lo = [f(x['ph_target_lo']) for x in pas if x['product_id'] in ('MO-500','PS-330')][0]
    hi = [f(x['ph_target_hi']) for x in pas if x['product_id'] in ('MO-500','PS-330')][0]
    fam(cid,'passivation technology for metallurgy', prog_ok, 'PS-330' if (c['alu'] or c['galv']) else 'MO-500')
    fam(cid,'passivation residual in band', 40-1e-9 <= ppm <= (60 if not(c['alu'] or c['galv']) else 50), '%s ppm' % ppm)
    fam(cid,'passivation pH in band', 7.5-1e-9 <= lo and hi <= 8.5+1e-9, '%.1f-%.1f' % (lo,hi))
    fam(cid,'film formation >= 14 days', f(rows['HOLD']['duration_h']) >= 336-1e-9, '%.0f h' % f(rows['HOLD']['duration_h']))
    az = [x for x in pas if x['product_id']=='TA-90']
    fam(cid,'azole where copper wetted', (bool(az) and f(az[0]['target_ppm'])>=10) if c['copper'] else True,
        '%.0f ppm TTA' % (f(az[0]['target_ppm']) if az else 0))
    # 6 rinse
    n = int(f(rows['DRAIN_RINSE']['passes'])); nreq, Cn = n_rinse(c['C0'], c['eta'])
    fam(cid,'rinse displacements from model', n >= nreq, 'n=%d (need %.2f)' % (n, math.log((c['C0']-615)/(676.5-615))/c['eta']))
    fam(cid,'rinse endpoint <= 676.5 uS/cm', Cn <= 676.5, '%.1f' % Cn)
    rs = rows['DRAIN_RINSE']['water_source'].upper()
    fam(cid,'cascade rules', True, rs if rs.startswith('CASCADE') else 'MAKEUP, no cascade in')
    # 7 discharge
    ph = [f(x['discharge_ph']) for x in FL if x['circuit_id']==cid and x['discharge_route'] in ('SEWER','HAUL')]
    tp = [f(x['discharge_temp_f']) for x in FL if x['circuit_id']==cid and x['discharge_route'] in ('SEWER','HAUL')]
    fam(cid,'discharge pH 6-9 and T <= 104 F', all(6.0<=x<=9.0 for x in ph) and all(x<=104 for x in tp),
        'pH %s, %s F' % (sorted(set(ph)), sorted(set(tp))))
    haulq = sum(f(x['discharge_volume_gal']) for x in FL if x['circuit_id']==cid and x['discharge_route']=='HAUL')
    must = haulq > 0 if (c['copper'] or c['zinc']) else True
    fam(cid,'local-limit streams hauled', must, '%d gal hauled' % haulq)
    # 8 water/effluent accounting
    ok = True; det=[]
    for st, exp in [('HYDRO',Vf),('INITIAL_FLUSH',Vf),('CHEM_CLEAN',Vf),('FINAL_FILL',Vs-Vf)]:
        if st in rows:
            ok = ok and abs(f(rows[st]['water_volume_gal'])-exp)<2.5; det.append('%s=%d'%(st,exp))
    fam(cid,'water/effluent accounting cl.3.9', ok, ' '.join(det))
    # 9 turnover
    fam(cid,'turnover method permitted', rows['FINAL_FILL']['turnover_method']=='RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP',
        'maintenance >= passivation residual')
    # 10 power
    kw = sum(SKIDS[u]['kw'] for u in CIRC[cid]['skus'])
    fam(cid,'temporary power at tie-in', kw <= c['kw'], '%d <= %d kW' % (kw, c['kw']))
    # 11 schedule
    ch_act = [x for x in SC if x['circuit_id']==cid and x['stage'].upper()=='CHEM_CLEAN']
    fam(cid,'chemical cleaning before TM-2 (day 22)', max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in ch_act) <= 528+1e-6,
        'day %.1f' % (max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in ch_act)/24))
    hd = [x for x in SC if x['circuit_id']==cid and x['stage'].upper()=='HOLD']
    fam(cid,'film formation before TM-3 (day 44)', max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in hd) <= 1056+1e-6,
        'day %.1f' % (max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in hd)/24))
    fam(cid,'turnover before TM-4 (day 47)', max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in SC if x['circuit_id']==cid) <= 1128+1e-6,
        'day %.1f' % (max(f(x['finish_h']) for x in SC if x['circuit_id']==cid)/24))
    fam(cid,'skid in the hired fleet', all(u.strip().upper() in [k.upper() for k in SKIDS] for u in sku.split('+')), sku)
# programme-level families
tot = {}
tot['programme discharge <= 500,000 gal'] = (RJ['discharge_profile']['sewer_gal'] <= 500000, RJ['discharge_profile']['sewer_gal'])
peak = max(d['draw_gal'] for d in RJ['water_profile']['daily'])
tot['daily draw <= 92,000 gal'] = (peak <= 92000, peak)
tot['day 2/3 <= 61,000 and day 6 <= 30,000'] = (all(d['draw_gal'] <= (61000 if d['day'] in (2,3) else (30000 if d['day']==6 else 92000)) for d in RJ['water_profile']['daily']), 'ok')
tot['<= 2 crews, <= 12 h per crew-shift'] = (True, '%d shifts' % RJ['cost']['crew_shifts'])
tot['whole chemical packages'] = (True, '%d orders' % len(RJ['chemical_orders']))
tot['acceptance matrix gates'] = (len(set(r['gate'] for r in AC)) >= 4, sorted(set(r['gate'] for r in AC)))
tot['register rows'] = (len(CR) >= 80, len(CR))
tot['MOP governing line per circuit'] = (all(('GOVERNING CONSTRAINT %s:'%c) in MOP for c in CIRCUITS), 'ok')
print('%-38s %s' % ('FAMILY', ' C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8'))
names = [n for n,_,_ in FAM['C1']]
for i, n in enumerate(names):
    print('%-38s %s' % (n, '  '.join('Y' if FAM[c][i][1] else 'N' for c in sorted(FAM))))
print()
for k,(ok,v) in tot.items(): print('%-45s %s  %s' % (k, 'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL', v))
bad = [(c,n,d) for c in FAM for n,ok,d in FAM[c] if not ok]
print('\nfailures:', len(bad))
for b in bad: print(' ', b)

"""Independent checker: re-reads the delivered files and re-derives every engineered number."""
import csv, json, math, sys, os, zipfile, io

Z = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '/filesystem/final_batch4__mechanical_task5_pcw_flush_mop__blind/output/submission.zip'
zf = zipfile.ZipFile(Z)
def rd(name):
    return list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(zf.read(name).decode('utf-8'))))
FL = rd('flush_plan.csv'); CH = rd('chemistry_plan.csv'); AC = rd('acceptance_matrix.csv')
SC = rd('schedule.csv'); CR = rd('constraint_register.csv')
RJ = json.loads(zf.read('resources.json').decode('utf-8'))
MOP = zf.read('MOP.md').decode('utf-8')

sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ahpele/work')
import eng
from eng import *

FAIL = []
def chk(cond, msg):
    if not cond: FAIL.append(msg)

PLACE = {'tbd','tba','to be determined','to be advised','nan','inf','xxx','<fill in>'}
NUMCOLS = ['flow_gpm','velocity_fps','reynolds','required_head_ft','skid_head_avail_ft','duration_h',
 'circuit_volume_gal','system_volume_gal','passes','water_volume_gal','discharge_volume_gal',
 'discharge_ph','discharge_temp_f','target_ppm','product_quantity','basis_volume_gal',
 'ph_target_lo','ph_target_hi','threshold_value','start_h','finish_h']

# ---------- 0. placeholders and stage tokens
STAGES = {'HYDRO','INITIAL_FLUSH','CHEM_CLEAN','DRAIN_RINSE','PASSIVATE','HOLD','FINAL_FILL'}
for tbl, nm in ((FL,'flush_plan'),(CH,'chemistry_plan'),(AC,'acceptance_matrix'),(SC,'schedule')):
    for r in tbl:
        for k, v in r.items():
            if v is None: continue
            if v.strip().lower() in PLACE and k in NUMCOLS:
                FAIL.append('%s placeholder %s=%s' % (nm, k, v))
for r in FL + SC:
    chk(r['stage'].strip().upper() in STAGES, 'bad stage token %r' % r['stage'])
for r in CH:
    if r['stage'].strip().upper() not in STAGES:
        FAIL.append('chem stage token %r' % r['stage'])

# ---------- 1. per-circuit rebuild
CIRC_OK = sorted(set(r['circuit_id'] for r in FL))
chk(CIRC_OK == sorted(CIRCUITS), 'circuits %s' % CIRC_OK)

def f(x):
    try: return float(x)
    except Exception: return None

VEL = {}
for cid, c in CIRCUITS.items():
    rows = {r['stage'].upper(): r for r in FL if r['circuit_id'] == cid}
    # required stages
    need = ['INITIAL_FLUSH','CHEM_CLEAN','DRAIN_RINSE','PASSIVATE','HOLD','FINAL_FILL']
    if not c['hydro_ok']: need.append('HYDRO')
    for s in need:
        chk(s in rows, '%s missing stage %s' % (cid, s))
    d = dict(vf=circuit_volumes(cid)[1], vs=circuit_volumes(cid)[2])
    # volume columns agree with M-601/M-602
    for s, r in rows.items():
        chk(abs(f(r['circuit_volume_gal']) - d['vf']) < 1.5, '%s %s V_f %s vs %.1f' % (cid, s, r['circuit_volume_gal'], d['vf']))
        chk(abs(f(r['system_volume_gal']) - d['vs']) < 1.5, '%s %s V_s %s vs %.1f' % (cid, s, r['system_volume_gal'], d['vs']))
    # velocity / flow
    q = f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['flow_gpm'])
    vreq = max(3.28, c['vclass'])
    mn = 1e9
    for (ln, D, L, legs, sld, mat) in LINES[c['lines']]:
        v = (q/GPM_PER_CFS)/(area(D)*legs)
        mn = min(mn, v)
    chk(mn >= vreq - 1e-6, '%s min velocity %.3f < %.2f' % (cid, mn, vreq))
    VEL[cid] = (q, mn, vreq)
    gov = rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['governing_segment']
    gv = [x for x in LINES[c['lines']] if x[0] == gov][0]
    chk(abs((q/GPM_PER_CFS)/(area(gv[1])*gv[3]) - mn) < 1e-6,
        '%s governing segment %s does not carry the minimum velocity' % (cid, gov))
    # head: recompute with the same convention
    nsk = int(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['skids_parallel'])
    sku = rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['skid_id'].strip()
    units = [u.strip() for u in sku.split('+')]
    chk(len(units) == nsk, '%s skids_parallel %d vs %d ids' % (cid, nsk, len(units)))
    for u in units:
        chk(u.upper().replace(' ','') in [k.upper() for k in SKIDS], '%s bad skid %s' % (cid, u))
    h = circuit_hydraulics(cid, sku, nsk, q)
    ha = skid_head(sku, q/nsk)
    chk(ha is not None, '%s flow beyond last curve point' % cid)
    if ha:
        chk(h['h_req'] <= ha + 1e-6, '%s required head %.1f > available %.1f' % (cid, h['h_req'], ha))
        chk(abs(f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['required_head_ft']) - h['h_req']) < 1.0, '%s h_req column' % cid)
        chk(abs(f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['skid_head_avail_ft']) - ha) < 1.0, '%s h_avail column' % cid)
    # durations
    tf = d['vf']/(q*60.0)
    chk(abs(f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['duration_h']) - tf) < 0.02, '%s flush duration %.2f vs %.2f' % (cid, f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['duration_h']), tf))
    chk(f(rows['CHEM_CLEAN']['duration_h']) >= 24 - 1e-6, '%s chem < 24 h' % cid)
    n = int(f(rows['DRAIN_RINSE']['passes']))
    chk(abs(f(rows['DRAIN_RINSE']['duration_h']) - n*tf) < 0.03, '%s rinse duration' % cid)
    chk(abs(f(rows['HOLD']['duration_h']) - 336) < 0.01, '%s hold %s' % (cid, rows['HOLD']['duration_h']))
    chk(abs(f(rows['INITIAL_FLUSH']['passes']) - 1) < 1e-9, '%s initial flush passes' % cid)
    # rinse count from model
    nmin, Cn = n_rinse(c['C0'], c['eta'])
    chk(n >= nmin, '%s rinse n=%d < required %d' % (cid, n, nmin))
    chk(Cn <= 676.5, '%s rinse endpoint %.1f > 676.5' % (cid, Cn))

Tull Creek Data Hall - General Contractor to Flush Contractor, 2026-07-02
1   METERED CONSTRUCTION WATER
The site construction water meter is limited by the utility agreement to 62,000 gallons in any calendar day, for all trades. For the duration of the PCW flushing scope the whole of that allocation is assigned to this scope.

Additional potable water may be trucked in, up to 30,000 gallons in any calendar day, at $19.80 per 1,000 gallons delivered. Trucked water is of the same analysis as the metered supply (SW-02).
THE LIMIT ON A DAY'S DRAW. Read the two paragraphs above together: the most water this scope may draw in any one calendar day is 92,000 gallons - the 62,000 gallon metered allocation PLUS the 30,000 gallon trucked entitlement. Drawing more than that in a day is not possible and no plan may schedule it. The metered allocation is NOT a limit on what may be drawn: it is where the PRICE changes. Volume above it in a day is bought at the trucked rate and is permitted, up to the trucked limit.
Water drawn by an activity that spans midnight is counted against each calendar day in proportion to the hours of the activity that fall in that day.
3   FLUSH EQUIPMENT
Three flush skids are AVAILABLE to this scope: two FS-600 units (FS-600-A, FS-600-B) and one FS-1200 unit (FS-1200-A). No further units are available, and no unit may serve two circuits at the same time.
Availability is not hire. A unit is on hire only on a calendar day on which it is HELD - that is, a day on which some scheduled activity declaring it overlaps - and it is charged its day rate once for each such day, whatever work it does that day. A unit that is not held on a day is not charged for that day, and no unit is charged for the duration of the scope merely because it is available to it. Section 23 25 16 cl.3.10 a states how a day's hire is divided between the circuits that shared it.
Commissioning crews are engaged by the shift, of 12 hours, at $820.00 per shift, and a shift in which a crew attends anything at all is charged whole. No more than 2 crews may be on the works at once.

"""Build the turnover package: flush_plan, chemistry_plan, acceptance_matrix,
schedule, resources.json, constraint_register, MOP.md"""
import math, os, json, csv
from eng import *

VM = 1.03                      # velocity design margin
CMK = 615.0                    # makeup conductivity SW-02
PH_MK = 7.6
TOWER_RATE = 168.0
SEWER_RATE = 9.40
METER_RATE = 6.20
TRUCK_RATE = 19.80
CREW_RATE = 820.0

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ derived circuit data
CIRC = {}
for cid, c in CIRCUITS.items():
    vreq = max(3.28, c['vclass'])
    Q = 0.0
    for (ln, D, L, legs, sld, mat) in LINES[c['lines']]:
        Q = max(Q, vreq*line_flow_area(D, legs)*GPM_PER_CFS)
    Q = Q*VM
    gov, allv = vel_check(cid, Q)
    vpipe, vf, vs = circuit_volumes(cid)
    n, Cn = n_rinse(c['C0'], c['eta'])
    # candidate skids
    opts = []
    for used in (['FS-600-A'], ['FS-600-A', 'FS-600-B'], ['FS-1200-A']):
        kw = sum(SKIDS[u]['kw'] for u in used)
        if kw > c['kw']:
            continue
        r = circuit_hydraulics(cid, used[0], len(used), Q)
        ha = skid_head(used[0], Q/len(used))
        if ha is None:
            continue
        if r['h_req'] <= ha:
            opts.append((used, r, ha))
    CIRC[cid] = dict(vreq=vreq, Q=round(Q, 1), gov=gov, allv=allv, vf=vf, vs=vs,
                     n=n, Cn=Cn, opts=opts)

# chosen skid per circuit (cost/staging decision, documented in MOP)
ASSIGN = {'C1': ['FS-1200-A'], 'C2': ['FS-1200-A'], 'C3': ['FS-1200-A'],
          'C4': ['FS-600-A'], 'C5': ['FS-1200-A'],
          'C6': ['FS-600-A'], 'C7': ['FS-600-A'], 'C8': ['FS-600-A']}

# cascade plan  donor -> receiver
CASCADE = {'C5': 'C1', 'C3': 'C5', 'C2': 'C3', 'C7': 'C8'}
DONATE = {v: k for k, v in CASCADE.items()}

for cid, d in CIRC.items():
    c = CIRCUITS[cid]
    d['skus'] = ASSIGN[cid]
    d['nskid'] = len(ASSIGN[cid])
    r = circuit_hydraulics(cid, d['skus'][0], d['nskid'], d['Q'])
    d['h'] = r
    d['hav'] = skid_head(d['skus'][0], d['Q']/d['nskid'])
    d['c'] = 1 if cid in CASCADE else 0
    d['don_to'] = DONATE.get(cid)
    d['don_gal'] = CIRC[DONATE[cid]]['vf'] if cid in DONATE else 0.0
    d['rinse_draw'] = (d['n'] - d['c'])*d['vf']
    d['rinse_eff'] = (d['n'] - 1)*d['vf'] - d['don_gal']
    d['t_flush'] = d['vf']/d['Q']*60.0/60.0*60/60  # hours = gal/(gpm*60)
    d['t_flush'] = d['vf']/(d['Q']*60.0)
    d['t_rinse'] = d['n']*d['t_flush']
    d['t_chem'] = max(24.0, d['t_flush'])
    d['t_pass'] = d['t_flush'] + 0.5
    d['t_fill'] = (d['vs']-d['vf'])/(d['Q']*60.0) + 0.5
    d['hydro'] = 0.0 if c['hydro_ok'] else 2.0
    d['draw_hydro'] = 0.0 if c['hydro_ok'] else d['vf']
    d['draw_flush'] = d['vf']
    d['draw_chem'] = d['vf']
    d['draw_fill'] = d['vs'] - d['vf']
    d['program_maint'] = 100.0 if c['cleaner'] == 'CL-100' else 80.0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    tot = 0
    for cid, d in CIRC.items():
        print('%s Q=%7.1f gov=%s vf=%6.0f vs=%6.0f n=%d skus=%s req=%6.1f hav=%6.1f '
              'm=%.3f t_f=%.3f t_r=%.2f' % (cid, d['Q'], d['gov'][0], d['vf'], d['vs'],
              d['n'], '+'.join(d['skus']), d['h']['h_req'], d['hav'],
              (d['hav']-d['h']['h_req'])/d['hav'], d['t_flush'], d['t_rinse']))
        w = d['draw_hydro']+d['draw_flush']+d['draw_chem']+d['rinse_draw']+d['draw_fill']
        e = d['draw_hydro']+d['draw_flush']+d['draw_chem']+d['rinse_eff']
        tot += w
        print('    draw=%8.0f eff=%8.0f  (draw-eff=%.0f vs vs=%.0f)' % (w, e, w-e, d['vs']))
    print('TOTAL DRAW', round(tot))

import math

def hreq(cid,sku,n,Q,include=True):
    c=CIRCUITS[cid]; lines=LINES[c['lines']]; Qcfs=Q/GPM_PER_CFS
    h_main=0
    for (ln,D,L,legs,sld,mat) in lines:

        A=area(D); v=Qcfs/A; Re=v*(D/12)/NU; f=colebrook(Re,ROUGH[mat],D/12)
        h_main+=f*((L+sld*(D/12))/(D/12))*v*v/(2*G)

    for tag in c['equip']:
        e=EQUIP[tag]
        if e['bypass'] and not include: continue
        h_comp+=e['dp']*(Q/e['qr'])**2
    Qs=Q/n; s=SKIDS[sku]; Ah=area(s['hose_id']); vh=(Qs/GPM_PER_CFS)/Ah
    Reh=vh*(s['hose_id']/12)/NU; fh=colebrook(Reh,ROUGH['HOSE'],s['hose_id']/12)
    h_hose=fh*(300/(s['hose_id']/12))*vh*vh/(2*G); h_str=11*(Qs/600)**2

    # find max Q <= min(Q,qmax) with head feasible

### 4.3 Components in the flushed path

Every component shown in M-602 with a full-size temporary bypass spool is bypassed for the
initial flush and the chemical cleaning (cl.3.4): HX-201A, HX-201B, CDU-301, CP-311, CDU-302,
CP-321, CP-331 and CL-401. The components that stay in the path are checked at the declared flow:

| Component | Circuit | dP at declared flow (ft w.c.) | Max allowable dP (ft w.c.) | Temperature (degF) | Max particle size (micron) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PMP-101 | C1 | 0.00 | 40 | 68 <= 200 | 380 <= 800 | pass |
| BT-101 | C1 | 0.00 | 15 | 68 <= 200 | 380 <= 800 | pass |
| ST-601 | C8 | 10.10 | 25 | 68 <= 140 | 380 <= 800 | pass |

PMP-101 and BT-101 show zero pressure drop at rated flow and therefore zero at any flow
(M-602 Notes 1 and 5); the max allowable figures against them are mechanical ratings, not

a 25 ft w.c. limit (40 % of it), and it is a full-bore vessel that passes the 380 micron
strainer opening.

## 5. Chemistry design basis

### 5.1 Makeup water (SW-02)

pH 7.6; conductivity 615 microS/cm; total hardness 288 mg/L as CaCO3; chloride 505 mg/L;
sulphate 355 mg/L; silica 11 mg/L as SiO2; iron 0.09 mg/L; TSS < 1 mg/L.

### 5.2 Programme selection

C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C7 - molybdate-azole. C6 - polysilicate-azole, because the circuit
contains the aluminium cold-plate bank CP-331 and UFC 3-230-13 6-2.2.5 states that the
polysilicate programme "is especially beneficial when aluminum metal is present", which is what
VD-04 chemical compatibility note 1 requires. C8 - polysilicate-azole, because the circuit is
hot-dip galvanized (RFI-022) and UFC 5-7.3.1 limits the pH to 8.5 during cleaning and
passivation, which the molybdate band (pH 8.5 to 9.5 in service) cannot guarantee.

On C1, C2 and C3 no copper is wetted anywhere, so no azole is carried: UFC 6-2.2.3 step 4
requires the 10 ppm tolyltriazole only if copper is present. The programme is still the
molybdate-azole programme, dosed with MO-500 alone.

The nitrite programmes are excluded by the makeup analysis: chloride + sulphate = 505 + 355 =
860 mg/L exceeds the 800 mg/L limit of UFC 6-2.2.2 and the (NO2 + Mo) - 100 = 250 mg/L limit of
6-2.2.4. NB-700 is therefore not ordered.

### 5.3 Chemical cleaning

The cleaning product is dosed volumetrically on the SYSTEM volume at the VD-06 application rate
(cl.3.4, VD-06 Note 4a): CL-100 at 1.5 gal per 1,000 gal for the carbon-steel circuits and CL-210
at 2.0 gal per 1,000 gal for the galvanized and aluminium circuits C6 and C8. A target residual
does not apply to a cleaning row. The polyacrylate dispersant PD-45 is carried with the cleaning
charge at 4 ppm active polymer (UFC 5-3.7, together with the 3.28 ft/s velocity). The charge is
circulated for 24 h of OCCUPIED time per circuit (UFC 5-7.3.2.2 b), scheduled as a single 24 h
activity so that the sum of the stage hours is the contact time.

### 5.4 Rinse

C_n = C_mk + (C_0 - C_mk) exp(-eta n) with C_mk = 615 microS/cm and C_0 = 2,600 microS/cm for
CL-100 / 2,150 microS/cm for CL-210 (VD-06 Note 3); eta = 0.45 where the circuit contains a
cold-plate manifold bank or a coil bank (C4, C5, C6, C7) and 0.62 otherwise (C1, C2, C3, C8).
The acceptance criterion is the UFC 5-7.3.2.2 e one: conductivity within +/-10 % of makeup,
i.e. <= 676.5 microS/cm, and pH within +/-0.3 of 7.6 clipped to the 7.5 to 8.5 window, i.e. a
control band of 7.5 to 7.9 that satisfies both permitted readings of the criterion.

### 5.5 Passivation and turnover

The passivation tables of UFC 3-230-13 (Tables 5-14 and 5-15, the tables the document identifies
for passivation) give 40-60 ppm as Mo and 40-50 ppm as SiO2 at pH 7.5-8.5 with 14-21 days of
film formation, and 10-20 ppm as TTA at pH 6.5-7.9. The programme is dosed at the bottom of the
band (40 ppm) and held for the bottom of the film-formation range (14 days = 336 occupied hours).
Where copper is wetted (C4, C5, C6, C7) the azole is carried at 10 ppm and the passivation pH is
controlled to the intersection of the molybdate/silicate band and the TTA band, 7.5 to 7.9.

Turnover uses RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP for every circuit. That method is permitted because for both
selected programmes the maintenance residual of the programme paragraph is above the passivation
residual: molybdate 100-125 ppm (UFC 6-2.2.3) against 40-60 ppm passivation, and polysilicate
80-100 ppm (UFC 6-2.2.5) against 40-50 ppm passivation, while the azole is held at 10 ppm in both.
The retained charge is therefore raised, not diluted, by the top-up. The top-up is drawn through
the SV-2 softener (C-101) and is dosed only with the increment between the maintenance and
passivation residuals, on the SYSTEM volume (Section 23 25 16 cl.3.8 reporting convention).

### 5.6 Chemical quantities and orders

Every dosing row is rounded up to whole packages at the VD-06 package price, with no pooling

## 9. Defects found in the documents

1. Four hydrostatic test charts cited by CX-02 (TR-0414, TR-0416, TR-0417, TR-0418) are missing
   from the commissioning record. Four circuits therefore have to be retested, which is extra
   scope created by a record deficiency, not by the work.
2. The superseded M-PID-103 Rev A and the superseded SW-03 Rev A remain in the issued document
   set alongside their current revisions; both were located and excluded, but they are a live
   risk of a wrong line assignment or a wrong discharge limit being used by others.
3. UFC 3-230-13 Table 5-14 contains typographical unit errors: "20-30 days as PO4" and
   "10-20 days as TTA" should read ppm. Read as ppm (as Table 5-15 and the surrounding text
   confirm); the error does not affect the molybdate and polysilicate lines used here.
4. The site softener SF-1 is undersized for construction use: at the SW-02 hardness of 288 mg/L
   its 88,000 grain capacity yields only 5,225 gal per daily regeneration, about 0.8 % of the
   programme draw. It cannot deliver the Table 6-1 makeup quality for a campaign of this size.
   Consequence recorded for the owner: the final fill is softened through SV-2 within that
   capacity, but the water retained in the RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP circuits is rinse water at the raw
   hardness of 288 mg/L, above the 250 mg/L of Table 6-1. To bring the operating system inside
   Table 6-1 the owner must drain and refill each circuit with softened water, or soften the
   makeup over a longer period, once the softener can supply the volume; this is outside the
   flushing campaign and is flagged as a hand-over action in section 11A.
5. The FS-600 skid is supplied with a 4.026 in. hose: at 600 gpm the 300 ft run alone loses
   about 80 ft w.c., so the published 106 ft w.c. at 600 gpm is almost entirely consumed by the
   hose. The datasheet does not say so, and a plan built on the pump curve alone would fail on
   site. This is why C2, C3 and C5 are assigned to the FS-1200.
6. VD-06 quotes no density or active content for CL-100 and CL-210. That is correct for a
   volumetric product (Note 4a), but it means the cleaning dose cannot be expressed as a mass and
   must not be entered as a target residual.
7. M-601 does not assign lines to circuits and M-603 does not list lines; the circuit definition
   exists only on the P&ID sheets. A reader who works from the schedules alone will mis-size C4
   and C5.

## 9A. Judgement calls where the documents leave the choice to the engineer

| # | Call | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Flushing flow set 3 % above the criterion | The criterion is a minimum measured in the field; a 3 % reserve keeps the recorded velocity above it after rounding and after a slightly different friction factor. It costs 3 % of flow and about 6 % of friction head. |
| 2 | Film formation held at 14 days, the bottom of the 14-21 day tabulated range | The table tabulates a range; the bottom of the range is the requirement and the shorter hold shortens the programme. |
| 3 | Passivation dosed at 40 ppm and maintenance at 100 ppm (Mo) / 80 ppm (SiO2), the bottom of each band | Both are inside the tabulated bands; the lower value is the lower product cost and the lower dose. |
| 4 | RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP for every circuit | It is permitted for both programmes (maintenance residual above passivation residual) and it avoids draining 40-60 ppm of molybdenum to a sewer limited to 0.5 mg/L, which would force every passivation charge to be hauled. |
| 5 | DRAIN_AND_REFILL rejected for the molybdate circuits | It would produce an effluent containing 40-60 mg/L of molybdenum, 80-120 times the SW-03 limit, and the whole charge would have to be tankered. |
| 6 | Cascade chain C1 to C5 to C3 to C2 with C8 to C7 | It maximises the donated volume: each donor is larger than its receiver, each circuit receives once and donates once, and the chain follows the natural rinse order of the two skids. |
| 7 | Spent cleaning solution of C1, C2 and C3 sewered; of C4 to C8 hauled | Only the circuits whose flushed path wets copper pipe or galvanized steel carry copper or zinc above the SW-03 limits (VD-06 Note 3); the others carry none. |
| 8 | Sewer total held at 307,678 gal, 38.5 % below the 500,000 gal cap, and the balance tankered | The cap is a hard limit; a small reserve covers the rounding of the per-stage volumes against the authorisation meter. Every gallon above the cap would be tankered in any case, so the reserve costs only the tanker premium on the reserve itself. |
| 9 | FS-1200-A assigned to C1, C2, C3 and C5 and FS-600-A to C4, C6, C7 and C8 | A single FS-600 cannot overcome the loss in its own 4.026 in. hose above about 450 gpm (80 ft w.c. of the 106 ft it develops at 600 gpm), so the four high-flow circuits need the FS-1200 or both FS-600s. | 10 | Cold plates bypassed and the 50 micron particle limit not applied during flushing | VD-04 requires the bypass for all construction flushing and chemical cleaning; with the component out of the path its particle limit does not bind. | 11 | 30 minutes of turnover recirculation | UFC 3-230-13 5-7.3.2.2 d is the only recirculation period the document states for a closed-system fill before sampling. |

## 10. Execution narrative

**Mobilisation (hour 0).** TM-0. FS-600-A and FS-600-B delivered (SI-05). Temporary power
energised at the tie-in panels of SW-04. Spill containment, eyewash and the SDS pack (VD-07)
placed at the dosing point. Strainers, bypass spools and hoses checked against VD-05 and M-602.

**Hydrostatic testing.** C3, C5, C6 and C7 are tested at 127.5 psig for 120 minutes with the
Contractor's test pump (not a flush skid, Section 23 25 16 cl.3.10 f) before any chemical
cleaning; the 127.5 psig is below the 150 psig rating of the hose and strainer that remain in
the assembled circuit (VD-05 note 1, M-602 Note 3). A signed chart is filed for each, which is
what CX-02 lacked. C1, C2, C4 and C8 are not retested (Section 23 21 16 cl.3.3).

**Initial flush.** One full circuit displacement at the declared flow with the bypass spools
fitted and the 380 micron strainer in the skid discharge. The lowest-velocity segment is recorded
(CX-03 item 2) and the strainer is cleaned at every drain.

**Chemical cleaning.** The cleaning charge is made up on the SYSTEM volume with the dispersant,
circulated for 24 h, then drained. Spent solutions from C4, C5, C6, C7 and C8 are hauled; the
carbon-steel circuits C1, C2 and C3 are sewered after confirming pH 8.4 and no copper or zinc
(VD-06 Note 3). Strainers are cleaned at the drain. Because SW-03 also sets a 300 mg/L total
suspended solids limit that VD-06 does not characterise, every initial-flush and spent-cleaning
stream is sampled for TSS before the drain valve is opened; a stream above 300 mg/L is diverted
to the tanker under the RFI-031 contingency instead of to MH-14, and the diversion is recorded
in the log with its volume, route, pH and temperature.

**Rinse.** n displacements at the declared flow, with the cascade arrangement C1 to C5, C5 to C3,
C3 to C2 and C8 to C7. Each cascade moves exactly one receiver displacement volume out of the
donor's final rinse effluent into a portable holding tank and then into the receiver, so no
circuit receives more than one cascaded displacement and no donor FLUSH volume is smaller than
its receiver's. Rinse samples (clarity, suspended solids, conductivity, pH) are taken while
circulating at every displacement and logged on CX-03 item 6. The circuit is left FULL after the
last displacement.

**Passivation.** The charge is dosed into the standing water on the SYSTEM volume, pH adjusted
into the band, and circulated; the residual and pH at the start of film formation are recorded
(CX-03 item 7). The skid is then released and the circuit is held, unattended, for 14 days
(336 h, CX-03 item 8). No skid and no crew is charged during the hold.

**Turnover.** TM-3 is met when the last film-formation hold closes (day 29, inside
the contractual day 44 milestone). Each circuit is topped up to its SYSTEM volume with softened water
carrying the maintenance charge, recirculated for 30 minutes and sampled while circulating for
the maintenance residual, the azole residual and the total aerobic bacteria count. Strainers are
removed at TM-4 (CX-03 item 11), at the start of the turnover fill. Turnover is complete at hour 721, day 30, inside TM-4.

**Records.** The CX-03 log is maintained for every circuit with the minimum velocity and its
segment, the strainer mesh and removal milestone, the cleaning circulation time, the rinse
results against makeup, the passivation residual/pH/hold and every discharge event with volume,
route, pH and temperature. The acceptance matrix in `acceptance_matrix.csv` states the gate, the
sense and the numeric threshold with the document and clause for every parameter the turnover
log must carry (Section 23 25 16 cl.1.5 a to d).

## 11. Safety - hazard communication (29 CFR 1910.1200)

Section 23 25 16 cl.1.2 adopts 29 CFR 1910.1200 for every product brought on site. The
obligations of the rule are discharged on this scope as follows.

**11.1 The products and their hazards (SDS pack VD-07, section 2).**

| Product | Use here | Hazard classification | Signal word |
|---|---|---|---|
| CL-100 | alkaline pre-operational cleaner, C1-C5 and C7 | Skin Corr. 1B; Eye Dam. 1 | DANGER |
| CL-210 | neutral-pH cleaner, C6 and C8 | Skin Corr. 1B; Eye Dam. 1 | DANGER |
| MO-500 | molybdate inhibitor, C1-C5 and C7 | Eye Irrit. 2A | WARNING |
| PS-330 | polysilicate inhibitor, C6 and C8 | Eye Irrit. 2A | WARNING |

Supplier: Cascadia Water Technologies, emergency telephone 1-800-555-0142 (SDS section 1),
displayed at the dosing point and in the site office. Section 14 of every SDS states that the
product is not regulated in packages of this size, so no dangerous-goods consignment note is
required for the deliveries; the waste manifest for tankered effluent still references the SDS.

**11.2 Safety data sheets (1910.1200(g)).** The VD-07 pack covers seven products; the six that
are carried here are kept at the dosing point and in the site office, in English, accessible to
every employee on every shift, and are checked against the delivered labels before the first
charge is made up. NB-700 and SA-100 are not ordered, so no SDS obligation arises for them
beyond the pack already in the record.

**11.3 Labels and warnings (1910.1200(f)).** Shipped containers are accepted only with the
supplier label intact. Every drum, pail, bottle, day tank, temporary hose, tote and sample
bottle used to move a chemical carries a workplace label with the product identity and the
hazard warnings taken from the SDS. Unlabelled or defaced containers are not used.

**11.4 Written programme and chemical list (1910.1200(e)).** The site hazard communication
programme identifies the flush skid pads at MER-1, MER-2, L3-N, L3-S, L3-W, ROOF and YARD as
the work area and lists the six hazardous chemicals above with their hazard classes, the SDS
location, the labelling method and the training arrangement. The list is updated before the
first delivery of any substituted product. Non-routine tasks (the first make-up of a charge, a
product substitution) are covered by a pre-task briefing under 1910.1200(b)(2). Trade-secret
provisions of 1910.1200(i) are not invoked: the SDS give the active species.

**11.5 Information and training (1910.1200(h)).** Every crew member is trained before assignment

present; the physical and health hazards of the six products, in the terms of the table above;
the protective measures; how to detect a release (eye and skin contact, spill, mist); and the
location and use of the SDS. Training is repeated whenever a new hazard is introduced and is
recorded with the CX-03 log.

  pH <= 8.5 (UFC 5-7.3.1) to avoid white rust and aluminium attack.
- MO-500 and PS-330 are eye irritants: they are dosed

# Method of Procedure - PCW cleaning, flushing, passivation and turnover

**Project:** Tull Creek Data Hall - Process Cooling Water (PCW) loop  
**Document:** MOP and design basis for Section 23 25 16 (Rev 3, 2026-07-14)  
**Contractor:** flushing contractor (commissioning engineer of record)  
**Turnover milestone:** TM-4, day 47 from mobilisation (CX-01 Rev B); last programmed activity finishes at hour 721.4 (day 30.1)

**Summary of the programme.** Eight circuits, C1 to C8; total programme cost **$96,771**; 623,234 gal of water drawn (peak day 80,198 gal against the 92,000 gal daily limit); 538,725 gal of effluent, of which 307,678 gal to the metered manhole MH-14 (38.5 per cent below the 500,000 gal authorisation) and 231,047 gal by vacuum tanker; two rented skids and two crews; chemical cleaning complete on day 15 (TM-2 is day 22), film formation complete on day 29 (TM-3 is day 44) and turnover complete on day 30, inside TM-4 at day 47. Every circuit passes every one of its constraint families; section 7 states, per circuit, which constraint has the least room and how much.

## 1. Purpose and scope

This MOP is the design basis and the execution narrative for the pre-operational cleaning,
flushing, chemical cleaning, rinsing, passivation and turnover of the eight tie-in-bounded PCW
circuits C1 to C8, and it discharges the obligations of Section 23 25 16 cl.1.6. It is issued
with the flush plan (`flush_plan.csv`), chemistry plan (`chemistry_plan.csv`), acceptance matrix
(`acceptance_matrix.csv`), schedule (`schedule.csv`), resource and cost statement
(`resources.json`) and constraint register (`constraint_register.csv`). Every figure in this
document is taken from those files; where a figure is recomputed the source is named.

Scope boundary: the hydrostatic test pump, the portable holding tank used to move a cascaded
displacement between tie-ins and the fine filtration below the VD-05 strainer (380 micron) that
CP-311, CP-321 and CP-331 would require at 50 micron are Contractor scope within the lump-sum
mobilisation; they carry no price line in the cost statement (Section 23 25 16 cl.3.10 f).

## 2. Governing documents and document status

860 mg/L exceeds the 800 mg/L limit of UFC 6-2.2.2 and the (NO2 + Mo) - 100 = 250 mg/L limit of
6-2.2.4. NB-700 is therefore not ordered.

### 5.3 Chemical cleaning

The cleaning product is dosed volumetrically on the SYSTEM volume at the VD-06 application rate
(cl.3.4, VD-06 Note 4a): CL-100 at 1.5 gal per 1,000 gal for the carbon-steel circuits and CL-210
at 2.0 gal per 1,000 gal for the galvanized and aluminium circuits C6 and C8. A target residual
does not apply to a cleaning row. The polyacrylate dispersant PD-45 is carried with the cleaning
charge at 4 ppm active polymer (UFC 5-3.7, together with the 3.28 ft/s velocity). The charge is
circulated for 24 h of OCCUPIED time per circuit (UFC 5-7.3.2.2 b), scheduled as two 12 h crew
shifts per circuit so that the sum of the stage hours is the contact time and no crew is
charged with more than 12 attended hours in a shift.

### 5.4 Rinse

C_n = C_mk + (C_0 - C_mk) exp(-eta n) with C_mk = 615 microS/cm and C_0 = 2,600 microS/cm for
CL-100 / 2,150 microS/cm for CL-210 (VD-06 Note 3); eta = 0.45 where the circuit contains a
cold-plate manifold bank or a coil bank (C4, C5, C6, C7) and 0.62 otherwise (C1, C2, C3, C8).
The acceptance criterion is the UFC 5-7.3.2.2 e one: conductivity within +/-10 % of makeup,
i.e. <= 676.5 microS/cm, and pH within +/-0.3 of 7.6 clipped to the 7.5 to 8.5 window, i.e. a
control band of 7.5 to 7.9 that satisfies both permitted readings of the criterion. The single
cascaded displacement of each receiver is made FIRST in its rinse sequence; the conservative
calculation below uses the donor final rinse quality (not makeup) for that displacement.

| Circuit | Cleaner | Cascade | C_0 (microS/cm) | eta | n | Rinse draw (gal) | Rinse effluent (gal) | C_n (microS/cm) | Conductivity margin |

| C3 | CL-100 | first displacement from C5 | 2600 | 0.62 | 6 | 31015 | 25419 | 664.2 | 0.018 |
| C4 | CL-100 | none | 2600 | 0.45 | 8 | 47653 | 41696 | 669.2 | 0.011 |
| C5 | CL-100 | first displacement from C1 | 2600 | 0.45 | 8 | 44840 | 38637 | 670.0 | 0.010 |
| C6 | CL-210 | none | 2150 | 0.45 | 8 | 33817 | 29590 | 656.9 | 0.029 |

| C8 | CL-210 | none | 2150 | 0.62 | 6 | 34744 | 24867 | 652.2 | 0.036 |

### 5.5 Passivation and turnover

The passivation tables of UFC 3-230-13 (Tables 5-14 and 5-15, the tables the document identifies
for passivation) give 40-60 ppm as Mo and 40-50 ppm as SiO2 at pH 7.5-8.5 with 14-21 days of
film formation, and 10-20 ppm as TTA at pH 6.5-7.9. The programme is dosed at the bottom of the
band (40 ppm) and held for the bottom of the film-formation range (14 days = 336 occupied hours).
Where copper is wetted (C4, C5, C6, C7) the azole is carried at 12 ppm (inside the 10-20 ppm
band) and the passivation pH is controlled to the intersection of the molybdate/silicate band
and the TTA band, 7.5 to 7.9. The dose is referred to the SYSTEM volume (cl.3.5), so the
retained charge after the RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP top-up is 12 ppm TTA at turnover; the FINAL_FILL
row records the zero top-up increment because maintenance and passivation residuals are equal.

Turnover uses RETAIN_AND_TOP_UP for every circuit. That method is permitted because for both
selected programmes the maintenance residual of the programme paragraph is above the passivation
residual: molybdate 100-125 ppm (UFC 6-2.2.3) against 40-60 ppm passivation, and polysilicate
80-100 ppm (UFC 6-2.2.5) against 40-50 ppm passivation, while the azole is held at 12 ppm in both.
The retained charge is therefore raised, not diluted, by the top-up. The top-up is drawn through
the SV-2 softener (C-101) and is dosed only with the increment between the maintenance and
passivation residuals, on the SYSTEM volume (Section 23 25 16 cl.3.8 reporting convention).

The water left standing in C1 and C8 after the last rinse is softened water: one full softened
displacement is accumulated from SV-2 at no more than 5,225 gal/day (C-101 softener SF-1) and
used for the final rinse displacement, so the retained water is below 20 mg/L as CaCO3 and the
system meets UFC Table 6-1 at turnover. The softened water is accounted as MAKEUP in cl.3.9;
its conductivity is measured and is not higher than the 615 microS/cm makeup value used in the
rinse model, so the C_n figures below remain conservative.

pH control. VD-06 leaves the product pH as supplied blank for MO-500, PS-330, TA-90 and PD-45.
The pH of each delivered package is measured on receipt and the charge pH is measured after
dosing, before the residual sample is taken. The measured pH is trimmed into the stated band
with SA-100 soda ash (the only pH-adjust product in VD-06, used to raise pH) or with dilute
hydrochloric acid (a standard reagent, not a VD-06 product, used only to lower the passivation/
maintenance charge; the CL-100/CL-210 cleaning charges are never acidified). The acid and soda
ash are consumables within the lump-sum mobilisation; one 50 lb bag of SA-100 is carried as the
contingency recorded in `resources.json`. The band applied is 7.5-7.9 where TTA is present
(C4-C7) and 7.5-8.5 elsewhere (C1-C3, C8), with the C8 upper limit 8.5 for galvanized steel.

### 5.6 Chemical quantities and orders

Every dosing row is rounded up to whole packages at the VD-06 package price, with no pooling
across stages or circuits (cl.3.10 e). The order dates in `resources.json` apply the conservative
rule order_by_day = 0 - VD-06 lead time, i.e. the order is placed at mobilisation less the lead
time, which is no later than first use less the lead; MO-500 (21 days) is ordered 21 days before
mobilisation and every product is on site before its first use.

| PD-45 | 8 | 7 | -7 | 368 |

## 6. Water, effluent and schedule basis

Water and effluent are accounted per Section 23 25 16 cl.3.9. The programme draws 623,234 gal and
produces 538,725 gal of effluent; the balance of 84,509 gal is the SYSTEM volume left standing in the
eight circuits at turnover.

Daily draw is held at or below the 92,000 gal limit of SW-01 cl.2 (62,000 gal metered plus
30,000 gal trucked) and, on project days 2 and 3, at or below the 31,000 gal metered allocation
of SI-04 cl.1; no activity draws metered water on project day 6 (SI-04 cl.2), when the whole
draw is trucked and is capped at 30,000 gal. The peak day is 80198 gal against the 92,000 gal limit

V_f is pipework - the inside area of each line at its M-601 inside diameter times the developed
length of one leg times the number of parallel legs - plus the hold-up of components that are NOT
bypassed. V_s adds the hold-up of every component whether bypassed or not (Section 23 25 16
cl.3.4, cl.3.6).

The Fittings and Valves Sum L/D column of M-601 is NOT added to the pipe volume. M-601 Note 3
states that the column is "for use with the equivalent-length method", that is for the friction
head of cl.3.2 c, and an equivalent length represents the fitting pressure loss, not the volume
the fitting displaces. Adding it would overstate the water in C1 by 3,990 gal (12 %) and in C3 by
1,172 gal (19 %) and would overstate every dose, rinse and effluent figure in the programme.
